clue.text: Please CO, surprisingly, serving up a thin slice of meat

indicators.note: letters arranged surprisingly have come out in an unexpected order

blocks.note: taken as written, the abbreviation included

explanation.surface: A commanding officer is politely asked to serve a thin cut of meat.
explanation.walkthrough: CO is the usual abbreviation for commanding officer, but here its two letters simply join the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: An escalope is a boneless piece of veal or pork beaten flat before frying.

clue.text: John's leaving a London location after eastern film star

taken as written

these letters are removed from the London district

explanation.surface: Someone called John moves out of a London district after an eastern film star arrives.
explanation.walkthrough: The eastern E comes first, then A, then St John's Wood with John's taken out, giving EASTWOOD.
explanation.definitionFit: Clint Eastwood is a famous Hollywood actor, best known for westerns and Dirty Harry.

clue.text: Lloyd Webber's instrument found in small room by orchestra's leader

indicators.note: the leader of a word is the letter at its front

blocks.note: a cell is a small room, as in a prison or monastery
first letter of orchestra

explanation.surface: A famous musician's instrument is discovered in a tiny room next to the orchestra's leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Julian Lloyd Webber, brother of the composer Andrew, is a well-known British cellist.
explanation.definitionFit: Julian Lloyd Webber made his career as a solo cellist, so the cello is the instrument he played.

clue.text: Loose-limbed Latin male gets under it

taken as written
he is the male pronoun

explanation.surface: A supple Latin man slips beneath something.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down answer, one piece getting under another means it is written below it in the grid.
explanation.definitionFit: Lithe means flexible and graceful, the same as moving with loose, easy limbs.

clue.text: American musician caught heading for historical French city with a royal

explanation.surface: An American musician is arrested on his way to an old French city with a member of royalty.

blocks.note: first letter of satirise
taken as written
the definite article

explanation.walkthrough: Reg Smythe drew the British comic strip Andy Capp. 'Article' here is the grammatical word, not a piece of writing.
explanation.definitionFit: Reg Smythe was the British strip artist who created Andy Capp in the Daily Mirror.

clue.text: Book a sail

blocks.note: first meaning: Ian Fleming's James Bond novel
second meaning: a small light sail set high above the skysail

explanation.walkthrough: Read as one phrase it sounds like reserving a sailing trip; it is two separate meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The title of a Fleming thriller is also the nautical name for a topmost square sail on a ship.

clue.text: Sense changes in a city in the Ruhr valley

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: It reads as praise for a Bond girl; in fact it is two meanings of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: Solitaire is the psychic heroine of a Bond story, and a solitaire is also one precious stone mounted on its own.

blocks.note: taken as written

blocks.note: folios are leaves of a book
standard abbreviation for female; this letter is removed

explanation.definitionFit: An olio is a spicy Spanish or Portuguese stew of meat and vegetables, a crossword favourite.

clue.text: Complete dive, reportedly

explanation.walkthrough: 'Dive' looks like a verb about plunging, but it is the noun for a disreputable venue.
explanation.definitionFit: Whole means entire or complete, with nothing missing.

clue.text: What a horse may have on coat so rain disperses

definitions.text: What a horse may have on

blocks.note: a cap is a covering layer on top, as in an ice cap, so a coat
taken as written

explanation.surface: A horse wears a waterproof coat so the rain runs off it.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue reads as a horse blanket keeping out rain, but coat is a mere layer and only the last two words are mixed.
explanation.definitionFit: A caparison is an ornamental cloth or harness draped over a horse, as worn by medieval chargers.

clue.text: Ephemeral insect - it may seen on the ground in summer

definitions.text: it may seen on the ground in summer

blocks.note: first meaning, whimsically: a chirping insect that lives just a day

blocks.clueFragment: it may seen on the ground in summer
blocks.note: second meaning: a limited-overs match played at a cricket ground in the summer season

explanation.walkthrough: The clue as printed drops 'be' from 'may be seen'. 'Ground' is a cricket ground, not the soil where insects live.
explanation.definitionFit: One-day cricket is the form of the game completed in a single day, and read literally the phrase is a short-lived insect.

clue.text: One who talks incessantly, here with Arabs, possibly

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A chatterbox may well be found here among Arabs.
explanation.walkthrough: 'With' simply joins the two words of fodder. An earbasher is Australian and British slang.
explanation.definitionFit: To earbash is slang for to talk at someone at length, so an earbasher is a relentless talker.

clue.text: A complete change of policy concerning revolution

blocks.note: about means concerning, on the subject of
a turn is a revolution, one rotation

explanation.definitionFit: An about-turn is literally a soldier's half-circle turn, and figuratively a reversal of opinion or policy.

clue.text: Medical complaint? Hint - iris affected

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A doctor's clue: the iris of the eye has been hit by some ailment.
explanation.walkthrough: The iris is part of the eye, steering the solver to an eye condition, but the answer is a nasal one.
explanation.definitionFit: Rhinitis is inflammation of the lining of the nose, as in hay fever or a cold.

clue.text: Reformed rascal met wise guy

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.definitionFit: A smart alec is an irritating know-all; a wise guy is the American term for the same person.

clue.text: A children's favourite may be followed by Barbara and Monica et al

explanation.definitionFit: Santa is the gift-bringer of Christmas, and Spanish for female saint in names such as Santa Barbara, Santa Monica and Santa Cruz.

clue.text: Right old racket made by French sculptor

blocks.note: a dell is a small wooded valley
standard abbreviation for wife

clue.text: A nob meeting a head of state too

taken as written
first letter of state
